## Task-routing table

One row per significant area of the repository. Because the repo is currently empty, most rows are `TODO`: they name the area an agent will need and mark it unresolved rather than inventing a convention that does not exist yet. **Fill each row in as the corresponding code lands** — a stale `TODO` is honest, an invented rule is not.

| When the task involves… | Read first | Key rules |
|---|---|---|
| The delivery process — labels, review loop, claim protocol, merge gates | `SDLC.md`, `.ai/agentic.config.json` | Pipeline labels are mutually exclusive; claim with all three signals before mutating an issue or PR; `qaGate` is off, so `needs-qa` is advisory. |
| Tracker operations — issues, PRs, comments, labels, merges | `.ai/trackers/github.md` | Never call `gh` for a tracker operation directly; every operation and label guard is defined in that descriptor. Edit the descriptor to change tracker behavior; all skills pick it up on their next run. |
| Browser automation — QA screenshots, E2E exploration | `.ai/browsers/agent-browser.md` | The descriptor owns provisioning and every browser operation (`open`, `snapshot`, `interact`, `assert`, `screenshot`, `close`). Local browser processes only; no cloud-browser account. Repository-native E2E suites, once they exist, remain authoritative over ad-hoc browsing. |
| Feature specifications and design docs | `.ai/specs/` (empty), `om-spec-writing` | Spec filenames are `{YYYY-MM-DD}-{kebab-case-title}.md`. A spec-only PR stays design-only; implementation ships on its own PR referencing it. |
| Autonomous run state — plans, handoffs, analysis reports | `.ai/runs/`, `.ai/analysis/` | Run folders are written by the loop skills and are the resume point for `om-auto-continue-pr[-loop]`; do not hand-edit a plan an active run owns. |
| Test environment bring-up and teardown | `.ai/scripts/` (empty), `.ai/qa/test-env.json` (not yet generated) | Generated by `om-prepare-test-env`. The launcher scripts are committed so the environment is reproducible; `test-env.json`, `test-env.env`, and `artifacts_*/` are generated per run and gitignored. |

## Validation commands

Run these in order before opening a PR or pushing a hand-worked branch. Any non-zero exit is a gate failure.

```bash
ruff check .
ruff format --check .
pytest
```

⚠️ **These are not yet installed.** They were configured as the intended Python gate for a repository that had no toolchain at setup time, not detected from a manifest. Until `ruff` and `pytest` are present and a test suite exists, expect the gate to fail on a missing executable. Add the toolchain and a `pyproject.toml` in the first substantive PR, or change `validation.commands` in `.ai/agentic.config.json` to match the stack the project actually adopts — and update this section and `SDLC.md` in the same change.

## Pointers

- `SDLC.md` — the ticket-to-merge process, label state machine, and claim protocol.
- `.ai/agentic.config.json` — the machine-readable configuration every `om-*` skill reads.
- `.ai/trackers/github.md` — the authoritative definition of every tracker operation; the repo's copy overrides the shipped one.
- `.ai/browsers/agent-browser.md` — the browser-automation contract.
- `.ai/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` — repo-local extension of an installed skill, for repo-specific rules. Local rules win on repo specifics but can never relax the installed skill's safety or quality rules.
- `CODE_REVIEW.md` — **not generated.** When added at the repo root it is picked up automatically by `om-code-review` and therefore `om-auto-review-pr`.
- `BACKWARD_COMPATIBILITY.md` — **not generated.** When added it defines the protected contract surfaces that review and implementation skills check changes against. Worth writing once this project exposes a public API, CLI, or schema.
